How limestone flows through the packer

2-spout stationary packer built in-house by the Maintenance Department

Path of the limestone

Tap a step to see it on the model.

  1. Feed pipeLimestone leaves the bin through the slide gates and runs down the inclined feed pipe.
  2. Into the centre tubeIt drops through the bolted top cover. Displaced air escapes up the vent and dust sock.
  3. Bent diaphragm plateThe stream lands on the ridge of the 45° plate and splits left and right, one half for each spout.
  4. Outlet and chuteEach half runs down to its outlet in the tube wall, then down through the tapered chute body into the housing.
  5. Impeller housingThe belt-driven impeller aerates the powder and throws it round the volute.
  6. Flow gateThe 3-position actuator holds the gate fully open for coarse fill, partly open for fine, or closed.
  7. SpoutAerated limestone runs along the spout and out of the discharge slot into the valve bag.
  8. Bag on the scaleThe empty bag is hung by its valve on the spout, standing on the scale, and the buffer clamps it. It swells through the timed coarse fill to about 40 kg and the fine top-up to 50 kg; then the clamp lifts and the bag is lifted off.

Survey model for illustration: dimensions are estimates and cycle times are shortened. The chips show the PLC outputs to the solenoid valves; the matching LEDs light on the manifold. The coarse time is set in the PLC, and the operator stops the fine fill at 50 kg.
